en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a hyperbola with foci $\mathrm{F}(c,\,0)$ and $\mathrm{F'}(-c,\,0)\ (c>0)$. For a point $\mathrm{P}$ on this hyperbola in the first quadrant, let $\mathrm{Q}$ be the point where segment $\mathrm{F'P}$ meets the $y$-axis, and let $\mathrm{R}$ be the point in the first quadrant where the line through the origin $\mathrm{O}$ parallel to segment $\mathrm{F'P}$ meets this hyperbola.

When $\overline{\mathrm{F'Q}}=\overline{\mathrm{QP}}$, $\overline{\mathrm{OQ}}=2$, and the area of triangle $\mathrm{PQR}$ is $3$, the length of the transverse axis of this hyperbola is $p+q\sqrt{13}$. Find the value of $p^{2}+q^{2}$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are rational numbers.) [4 points]
